A comprehensive Korean program designed to teach Korean language through real-life situations! A global initiative featuring top performers. Benefit from clear and friendly explanations by Peter Vint, a British TV personality who mastered Korean himself. Engage in lively Korean language lessons taught by Korean-American idols Aaron and Alexa! Experience a delightful Korean language course that delves into culture, trends, and even generational nuances. Each lesson is a concise 10-minute package, including scenarios, explanations, and practical exercises. It also covers traditional Korean culture and essential travel information, making it an invaluable resource for beginner to intermediate learners! Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. With clear and accessible explanations from Hye-rim of the Wonder Girls, a graduate of Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, you?ll systematically improve your Korean!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.title: SMARTBIZ ACCELERATORS(30?)
channel.desc: Along with the strengthened manufacturing capabilities of various countries all around the world, \"Smart Factory\" has garnered a lot of attention in the global market. Moreover, a domestic major company Samsung Electronics has provided a smart factory solution in order to boost mutual growth with small and medium-sized businesses. channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.title: DECODED: THE AI CONVERSATIONS
channel.desc: AI is no longer a technology of the future; it is a current reality reshaping our daily lives and entire industries. Korea, in particular, is one of the countries most dynamically experiencing this change, as AI deeply penetrates various sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, and manufacturing. Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. This journey features Dr. Kang Sung-ju, also known as the science communicator \"Hang sung\", as a fixed panelist. In the conversation among the MC, the panelist, and the guests, complex AI concepts are naturally \"decoded\" into everyday language. This will be a platform that vividly delivers the frontline of AI innovation where technology, industry, and policy intersect.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DIPLOMAT'S ARCHIVE: HIDDEN STORIES
channel.desc: As of April 2025, S. Korea has established diplomatic relations with a total of 194 countries. Among them are countries that have had ties and exchanges with Korea for hundreds of years. With such long-standing relationships with so many nations, might there be fascinating hidden stories between Korea and the rest of the world that we don?t know yet? \"Diplomat?s Archives: Hidden Stories\" begins with this very question. Together with foreign embassies in Korea, the series uncovers and sheds light on meaningful yet lesser-known stories between Korea and other countries. Through this, we aim to reaffirm the deep friendships that have been built over time, highlight how countries are interconnected?bilaterally and multilaterally? and emphasize the importance of cooperation on the global stage today.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: RPG
channel.desc: What is it like to love in Korea? Where do people usually go on dates, and what makes K-romance unique? (Romantic Path Guide) is a reality dating show where a foreign participant experiences love and dating in Korea while exploring its iconic landmarks. With fun missions to complete, encounters to discover, and moments to share, it?s a journey that feels just like playing an ? only this time, in real life. A mix of travel, culture, and romance. Step into the adventure and discover the path to love in Korea!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Almanacco di Bellezza
channel.desc: Il meglio dalle edizioni passate di Almanacco di Bellezza. Piero Maranghi insieme a Leonardo Piccinini, passa in rassegna, anniversari e ricorrenze legati al mondo dell'arte, della cultura, della storia e dello sport.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: La classica domanda: Stefano Boeri
channel.desc: Continuano le interviste di Anton Giulio Onofri a personalita' del mondo della cultura, dello spettacolo e dell'arte italiana - Ospite di questa puntata della Classica domanda e' l'architetto Stefano Boeri.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Concerto dal Duomo di Santo Stefano
channel.desc: Musiche di Mozart, Bach, Schubert, Haendel e i piu' bei canti dell'Avvento per il concerto nel Duomo di Santo Stefano a Vienna, simbolo e capolavoro gotico \(Wiener Stephansdom, 2025\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Mascagni - Cavalleria Rusticana
channel.desc: Versione cinematografica girata nel 1981 dell'opera in unico atto \(1892\) - con E.Obraztsova, P.Domingo, R.Bruson, F.Barbieri - Orchestra e Coro del Teatro alla Scala - George Pretre, dir. - Franco Zeffirelli, reg.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Leoncavallo - Pagliacci
channel.desc: Versione cinematografica girata nel 1982 dell'opera in due atti \(1892\) - con P.Domingo, T.Stratas, J.Pons, R.Bruson, E.Obraztsova - Orchestra e Coro del Teatro alla Scala - Georges Pretre, dir. - Franco Zeffirelli, reg.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Schubert - Quintetto D.956
channel.desc: La Kremerata Baltica diretta da Gideon Kremer esegue, nella versione per orchestra d'archi, il Quintetto in do maggiore op.163, ultimato nel 1828 a pochi mesi dalla morte dell'autore \(Salisburgo, 2002\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Joyce DiDonato - Eden in Olympia
channel.desc: Arie da Cavalli e Haendel fino a Charles Ives - Il Pomo d'Oro - Coro voci bianche Opera Nazionale Greca - El Sistema Greece Youth Choir - Eclats,Choeur d'enfants et de jeunes - M.Emelyanychev, dir. \(Archea Olympia, 2024\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Mestiere Teatro
channel.desc: Un viaggio alla scoperta di quanti nei teatri, lontano dalla ribalta, in ufficio, nei laboratori, dietro le quinte, nella buca, lavorano per la riuscita e il successo di uno spettacolo. A cura di Paolo Gavazzeni.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Notevoli - Antonio Moscheni
channel.desc: Documentario sul pittore italiano e gesuita Antonio Moscheni, ricordato come 'Michelangelo indiano' per gli affreschi a Mangalore, in India - con C.Modolo, S.Tangorra - regia di C.Piti' su soggetto di S.Rizzi \(2025\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Pianisti - L'Accademia di Imola, ep.5
channel.desc: Far suonare il fortepiano' - quinta puntata della serie Pianisti che svela i dietro le quinte dell'Accademia di Imola: attivita', grandi concerti, sfide, tensione e dedizione - con Jin Ju - G.De Stefano, reg. \(2015\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Maurice Ravel - Schegge musicali
channel.desc: Viaggio musicale sulla vita e le composizioni di Ravel - con M.L.Garnier, S.Devieilhe, B.Chamayou, C.O.Bensaid, R.Moreau - Orchestre de Paris, Quatuor Modigliani - Francois-Rene' Martin, reg., Klaus Makela, dir. \(2025\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Gala Monteverdi
channel.desc: Concerto per celebrare l'arte musicale e teatrale di Claudio Monteverdi - con R.Villazon, M.Kozena, T.Lehtipuu, K.Watson - Le Concert d'Astree - E.Haim, dir. \(Theatre des Champs Elysees, Parigi - 2014\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: La Classica domanda - Ruggero Cappuccio
channel.desc: Proseguono le interviste condotte da Anton Giulio Onofri a personalita' del mondo della cultura, dell'arte e dello spettacolo. Ospite della Classica domanda e' il drammaturgo e regista teatrale Ruggero Cappuccio.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Almanacco di Bellezza
channel.desc: Piero Maranghi, direttore di Sky Classica, passa in rassegna, anniversari e ricorrenze legati la mondo dell'arte, della cultura, della storia e dello sport. In studio con lui, il collezionista ed esperto d'arte Leonardo Piccinini.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Dvorak - Sinfonia n.9
channel.desc: Composta ed eseguita per la prima volta a New York nel 1893, la Sinfonia n.9 in mi minore e' detta Dal nuovo mondo - Berliner Philharmoniker - Gustavo Dudamel, dir. \(Philharmonie, Berlino - 2017\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Goldberg Variations
channel.desc: Balletto \(2018\) sulle Variazioni Goldberg di Bach - con E.Bottaro, O.Esina, H.J.Kang, L.Konovalova, C.Schoch - W.Youn, pianoforte - Wiener Staatsballett - H.Spoerli, coreografia e regia \(Vienna, Staatsoper - 2023\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Yuri Temirkanov e Yuja Wang
channel.desc: Concerto diretto da Yuri Temirkanov con la Verbier Festival Orchestra e la pianista Yuja Wang - In programma: Kikimora di A.Lyadov, Concerto per pianoforte n.2 di Rachmaninov, ed estratti da 'Il Lago dei cigni' di Cajkovskij \(2011\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Torino sei Regio! - Capodanno 2026

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Generali 190: Persone e Storie - 1831

channel.title: The World Heritage Sites In Japan
channel.desc: Mt. Fuji is Japan's tallest and most famous peak. As an active volcano, it has also inspired awe and terror. Mt. Explore the beauty of a mountain that inspires both artists and faith.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Nun's Seasonal Calendar
channel.desc: Join us as we learn about life at the Otowasan Kannonji Temple through 24 terms from the solar calendar. Then, we follow them on Shoman as they serve mehari-zushi (eye-popping sushi) to villagers who helped clean up the mountain paths ahead of the rainy season.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Train Cruise
channel.desc: We journey through the snowy landscapes of northern Fukui Prefecture in central Japan on the Echizen Railway. The local trains, which are a lifeline for residents, operate over a total distance of 53 kilometers and provide access to many sightseeing locations. Visit the 770-year-old Eiheiji and practice zazen meditation, sip locally brewed sake and dine on Echizen crab, as we train cruise through the natural winter wonderland of the old Echizen Province on the Sea of Japan.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Info
channel.desc: No description available.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Japanology Plus Mini
channel.desc: Japanese paper, known as washi, is attractively textured and extremely durable. In Japan, it's used in everything from sliding doors to banknotes. Paper first arrived from China around the 7th century and spread alongside Buddhism. Recently, crafts featuring washi have been getting attention outside Japan, and new paper production methods?including using vegetable scraps?have been popping up. In a 5-minute digest, we explore washi's role in modern society and examine how it represents Japanese aesthetics.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: In Saidaiji Eyo, a matsuri in Okayama Prefecture, thousands of near-naked men endure icy water and the winter cold as they are purified at the temple. This is part of one of Japan's most prominent \"naked\" festivals. Usually, the men scramble to grab one of two sacred wooden items called shingi, but the event was hit hard by COVID-19. Gradually, the normal rites are being reintroduced, and this time the public can view the climax. They enjoy performances of dancing and taiko drumming, as well as a firework display.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Darwin's Amazing Animals
channel.desc: The beautiful spotfin lionfish is also known as the \"Lady of the Sea\". Its flashy red and white stripes and long spines extending from the body make it instantly recognizable. But don't let the graceful appearance fool you. These fish are in fact extremely poisonous. The long fins contain venom that protects them against enemies. Their hunting style is also unique. They use their fins like feet to sneak up on their prey and swallow it whole with unbelievable speed. Shot in the waters of the Philippines, this episode reveals the amazingly deceptive nature of these graceful beauties.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Time Lapse Journey
channel.desc: Iwate Prefecture is home to many historic sites which were made to represent Buddhist paradise. Chuson-ji Temple in Hiraizumi, a World Heritage Site, is home to the golden Konjikido hall which offers a prayer for peace. The garden in Motsu-ji Temple was made as a depiction of paradise and has been also registered as a World Heritage Site. Catch a glimpse of eternity through time-lapse photography.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Japanology Plus Mini
channel.desc: For hundreds of years, Japanese people have used name stamps, known as hanko, to sign their name. People use hanko in everyday situations, such as receiving a parcel, and in formal contexts, such as business transactions and marriage registrations. However, the move toward remote work, triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic, affected how these stamps were used. In a 5-minute digest, we discover the history of hanko and explore what a hanko-free future might look like.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Easy Japanese For Work
channel.desc: The second in a special two-part EJW series. On Easy Japanese for Work, we've looked at many Japanese phrases that people use at work. Today, we'll review past phrases and learn Keego through some fun games. First, reviewing past key phrases. Past students and some of their coworkers join us to learn new phrases through a quiz. Today's students are from the Philippines and Vietnam. They must work together to come up with Japanese phrases. Next, at Keego Corporation, a fill-in-the-blank style quiz. How will our students do? Tune in to find out.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Zero Waste Life
channel.desc: \"They're not trash cans, but resource bins,\" says Murakami Yuki. His love of making goes back to childhood. And at college he developed his own banana peel leather. Transforming garbage and scrap into useful materials?? lampshades from coffee grounds or chairs from old receipts?? his creations are unique, but they're also as biodegradable as possible, with minimal environmental impact. This sort of alchemy has earned praise and serious interest from industries facing issues surrounding waste.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Japanology Plus Mini
channel.desc: For hundreds of years, Japanese people have used name stamps, known as hanko, to sign their name. People use hanko in everyday situations, such as receiving a parcel, and in formal contexts, such as business transactions and marriage registrations. However, the move toward remote work, triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic, affected how these stamps were used. In a 5-minute digest, we discover the history of hanko and explore what a hanko-free future might look like.
